entries.name: DefCardinality
entries.title: Class cardinality
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(K:Class)(|K|=(On∩⋂{a|(a∈On)∧(K≼a)})))
entries.comment: Defines the von Neumann initial-ordinal cardinality |K| = On ∩ ⋂{ a : Class | (a ∈ On) ∧ (K ≼ a) }: the intersection ⋂ of the class of all ordinal sets a ∈ On into which K injects (K ≼ a), intersected with On. Because the intersection of a non-empty class of ordinals is its least element, |K| equals the least ordinal a ∈ On with K ≼ a (the initial ordinal of K) when K is a well-orderable set, and equals On ∩ ⋂∅ = On ∩ V = On when no ordinal set a ∈ On satisfies K ≼ a (i.e., when K is a proper class). Paired in the kernel with CardLessOrderAx (PCardLessOrderAx_prf in 06_definitions.ML: ∀A∀B((|A| ≺ |B|) ⟷ (A ≺ B))).

entries.name: DefCardLess
entries.title: “Is strictly smaller than” binary relation
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)((A≺B)←→(¬(B≼A))))
entries.comment: Strict cardinality order A ≺ B ⟷ ¬(B ≼ A). Paired in the kernel with the cardinal-order reflection rule CardLessOrderAx (PCardLessOrderAx_prf in 06_definitions.ML: ∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)((|A| ≺ |B|) ⟷ (A ≺ B))), which embodies the Global Choice / von Neumann cardinal-equipollence principle |K| ≈ K connecting 3.41 DefCardinality with 3.43 AxmSizeLimitation.

Combined with the kernel's cardinal-order reflection rule CardLessOrderAx (PCardLessOrderAx_prf: (|A| ≺ |B|) ⟷ (A ≺ B), reflecting Global Choice V ≈ On), this yields (X ∈ V) ⟷ (X ≺ V) and hence Tight(V) in 3.69.

entries.name: DefOmega
entries.title: The intersection class of all successor-inductive (Peano-inductive) classes is called omega (⊆-minimal successor-inductive class and smallest successor-inductive ordinal)
entries.status: Definitional (Conservative Under Set Existence, Kernel AST)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(x:Class)((x∈ω)←→(∀(Q:Class)(Ind(Q)—→(x∈Q)))))
entries.comment: By definition, ω is not only the smallest successor-inductive ordinal, but also the ⊆-minimal (least) element among all successor-inductive (Peano-inductive) classes in the subclass (⊆) order (Ind(ω) ∧ ∀(Q:Class), Ind(Q) —→ (ω ⊆ Q)), directly expressing simple countable mathematical (Peano) induction up to ω. Conservativity & Sethood Note: because (x ∈ Q) implies (x set) by 3.02 DefIsSet whenever at least one inductive class Q exists (such as On in 3.60 or ω under 3.57 AxmOmegaIsSet), the unguarded RHS ∀(Q:Class)(Ind(Q) —→ x ∈ Q) is equivalent in MKTD1-theory to the strict comprehension form ((x set) ∧ ∀(Q:Class)(Ind(Q) —→ x ∈ Q)); however, in a subtheory without set-existence axioms, omitting (x set) on the RHS makes ∅ ∈ ω (and hence ∅ set) derivable from DefOmega and DefInductiveClass alone. In our kernel proofs (universe_definitions.ML), ∅ set is derived explicitly from 3.57 AxmOmegaIsSet (ω set), 3.07 (∅ ⊆ ω), and 3.12 AxmHeredity. Similarly, the set-restricted intersection ω = ⋂{q | Ind(q)} over inductive sets q agrees with the general intersection over all inductive classes Q once an inductive set exists by 3.57 AxmOmegaIsSet. | Special Def.: ω = ⋂{q | Ind(q)} (set-restricted intersection over inductive sets, equivalent to the general form once an inductive set exists by 3.57 AxmOmegaIsSet); General Def.: ∀(x:Class), (x ∈ ω) ⟷ (∀(Q:Class), Ind(Q) —→ (x ∈ Q)).

entries.name: ThmOmegaCardinal
entries.title: ω is cardinal
entries.formula_unicode_html: Card(ω)
entries.comment: Kernel proof term thm_3_65_omega_cardinal (types/omega_cardinal.ML, exact statement Card(ω)): by 3.64 DefIsCardinal with K := ω it suffices that |ω| = ω (3.41 DefCardinality). |ω| ⊆ ω because ω ≼ ω, witnessed by the identity {p | ∃k((k ∈ ω) ∧ (p = (k, k)))}, an injective class function (Dunaev pairs of sets are sets, as subclasses of 𝒫⁴(k)). ω ⊆ |ω| combines two inductions: every ordinal a satisfies n ∈ a or a ⊆ n for n ∈ ω (EpsIndAx), and the finite pigeonhole principle ¬(ω ≼ n) for n ∈ ω (induction on n over classes X with no ∈-maximal element, so no new functions are built).

entries.name: ThmOrdinalsCardinal
entries.title: On is a cardinal class
entries.formula_unicode_html: Card(On)
entries.comment: Kernel proof term (thm_3_66_on_card_sub_on : Thm with exact statement equality): proves (On cardinal) by taking K := V as the witness in 3.64 DefIsCardinal (∃K(|K| = On)). For every a ∈ S_V = {a | (a ∈ On) ∧ (V ≼ a)}, a ∈ On implies a set (3.02 DefIsSet) and hence a ∈ V (3.05 DefUniversalClass), which by 3.43 AxmSizeLimitation (PSizeLimAx_prf), CardLessOrderAx (PCardLessOrderAx_prf), and 3.42 DefCardLess yields a ≺ V ⟷ ¬(V ≼ a), contradicting V ≼ a. Hence S_V is empty, every x ∈ On belongs to ⋂S_V (3.20 DefUnaryIntersection), |V| = On ∩ ⋂S_V = On (3.41 DefCardinality, 3.10 DefClassEq), and therefore Card(On) holds.

entries.name: AxmSoundnessOfFullTheory
entries.title: Soundness of the theory 𝘍
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(𝛗:Fm)((𝘍,[]⊢𝛗)—→eval(𝛗)))
entries.comment: Soundness of the non-r.e. theory of the intended model 𝘍: if (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ), then ⟦φ⟧ holds in the fixed background model M. Two-Level Stratification (How the Kernel Excludes TpHolds(IpFau, ...) from Object-Level Fm₀): In MKTD1-system (FACTBOOK section 6 (metalevels)), object-level set/class formulas live at metalevel 0 (sort Fm₀, enforced in the kernel by KernelDefinitions.is_object_level_fm0 in newchecker/06_definitions.ML and checked on every PComprAx_prf class comprehension node in newchecker/07_theorems.ML), which explicitly rejects TpHolds, EEval, TpFFI, TpIFV, and TpCtxIFV inside object-level class comprehension {x | φ} and object-level predicate/class definitions. Because 3.72-3.74 and 4.03 live at metalevel +1 and TpHolds(IpFau, ...) is barred from Fm₀ comprehension by is_object_level_fm0, the object-level diagonal lemma cannot be applied to (𝘍, [] ⊢ ·) to form a Tarski liar sentence or a Löb fixed point ψ ⟷ ((𝘍, [] ⊢ ψ) —→ φ).

entries.title: Semantic Completeness of the theory 𝘍
entries.status: Metatheorem (Holds by the Definition of F, Not a Kernel Rule)
entries.prf_constructor: (metatheorem: holds by the definition of F; not a kernel rule)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(𝛗:Fm)(eval(𝛗)—→(𝘍,[]⊢𝛗)))
entries.comment: Semantic completeness (omniscience, 3.73) of the non-r.e. theory of the intended model 𝘍 at metalevel 1: for every object-level sentence φ : Fm, if φ evaluates to true in the background model M (⟦φ⟧), then φ is formally derivable in 𝘍 (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ). It holds by the definition of 𝘍 as the theory of the intended model (FACTBOOK section 2) and is a metatheorem, not a kernel rule. Stated separately from syntactic negation-completeness (3.74 AxmNegationCompletenessOfFullTheory, which is stated purely in terms of ⊢ and ¬ without mentioning ⟦φ⟧): neither implies the other in isolation, while under Soundness of 𝘍 (3.72) and classical model bivalence (⟦φ⟧ ∨ ⟦¬φ⟧) they are conditionally equivalent.

entries.title: Ordered pair(Dunaev's tagged class pair)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)((A,B)=(({{∅,{∅}}}∪{x|∃(a:Class)((a∈A)∧(x={{{{a}}},{∅}}))})∪({{∅,{∅,{∅}}}}∪{x|∃(a:Class)((a∈B)∧(x={{{{a}}},{∅,{∅}}}))}))))
entries.comment: Primitive-expanded form of Dunaev's tagged class ordered pair (A,B) = mark(A,1) ∪ mark(B,2) from 3.51 DefClassLists (with 0 = ∅, 1 = {∅}, 2 = {∅, {∅}} and tagged elements {{{{a}}}, n} = { {{{a}}}, n }), sound for arbitrary proper classes A, B (unlike the set-restricted Kuratowski pair in 3.52). Used as the canonical ordered pair (A, B) across class-level definitions (3.38, 3.77, 3.78, 3.91).

entries.name: ThmDunaevFirstProjection
entries.title: First projection of Dunaev's tagged ordered pair
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)({a|{{{{a}}},{∅}}∈(A,B)}=A))
entries.comment: Kernel proof term (thm_3_77_dunaev_pr1_sub : Thm with exact statement equality): recovers A from Dunaev's tagged ordered pair (A, B) via tag 1 = {∅} ({ a | {{{{a}}}, {∅}} ∈ (A, B) } = A, matching pr1 in 3.51 DefClassLists and 3.91 DefDomainRestriction) without requiring A or B to be sets, and together with 3.78 yields Dunaev pair injectivity (thm_dunaev_opair_injective : (A, B) = (C, D) —→ (A = C ∧ B = D)).

entries.name: ThmDunaevSecondProjection
entries.title: Second projection of Dunaev's tagged ordered pair
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)({b|{{{{b}}},{∅,{∅}}}∈(A,B)}=B))
entries.comment: Kernel proof term (thm_3_78_dunaev_pr2_sub : Thm with exact statement equality): recovers B from Dunaev's tagged ordered pair (A, B) via tag 2 = {∅, {∅}} ({ b | {{{{b}}}, {∅, {∅}}} ∈ (A, B) } = B, matching pr2 in 3.51 DefClassLists) without requiring A or B to be sets, and together with 3.77 yields Dunaev pair injectivity (thm_dunaev_opair_injective : (A, B) = (C, D) —→ (A = C ∧ B = D)).

entries.name: DefLimitOrdinal
entries.title: Nonzero limit ordinal predicate
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Class)(LimitOrd(A)←→(Ord(A)∧((¬(A=∅))∧∀(B:Class)((B∈A)—→((B∪{B})∈A))))))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefLimitOrd, PKernelDef_prf): a class A is a nonzero limit ordinal (LimitOrd(A)) iff A is an ordinal, A is non-empty, and for every B in A, the von Neumann successor B u {B} also belongs to A.

entries.name: DefIndexedUnionClosed
entries.title: Indexed-union closure predicate
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(U:Class)(IndexedUnionClosed(U)←→(∀(I:Class)∀(f:Class)(((I∈U)∧((f class-function)∧((I⊆Dom(f))∧(f[I]⊆U))))—→(⋃f[I]∈U)))))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefIndexedUnionClosed, PKernelDef_prf): a class U is closed under indexed unions (IndexedUnionClosed(U)) iff for every index set I in U and every class-function f with I c Dom(f) and relational image f[I] c U, the union U(f[I]) belongs to U.

entries.name: DefVonNeumannStageLaws
entries.title: Von Neumann cumulative hierarchy recursion laws
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(V:Class)(VStageLaws(V)←→((V(∅)=∅)∧((∀(A:Class)(Ord(A)—→(V((A∪{A}))=𝒫(V(A)))))∧((∀(A:Class)(LimitOrd(A)—→(V(A)=⋃{Y|∃(B:Class)((B∈A)∧(Y=V(B)))})))∧∀(A:Class)(Ord(A)—→((A=∅)∨((∃(B:Class)((B∈A)∧(A=(B∪{B}))))∨LimitOrd(A)))))))))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefVonNeumannStageLaws, PKernelDef_prf): VStageLaws(V) characterizes the transfinite recursion equations for the von Neumann cumulative hierarchy stages valOf(V, A) across base stage 0, successor ordinals A u {A}, and limit ordinals, together with the three-way ordinal classification (zero, successor, or limit). (Notational convention: here and in 3.82, 3.83, 3.88, 3.89, 3.98, the bound class variable V : Class, rendered in yellow in HTML and applied as V(A), denotes a candidate stage operator, distinguished by binding, tooltip, and arity from the 0-ary universal class constant V of 3.05 and 3.86.)

entries.name: DefVonNeumannStageGraph
entries.title: Canonical von Neumann cumulative hierarchy graph
entries.formula_unicode_html: (VStageGraph=⋂{V|(V class-function)∧VStageLaws(V)})
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefVonNeumannStageGraph, PKernelDef_prf): VStageGraph is the intersection of all class-functions V satisfying VStageLaws(V). Restricting V to class-functions (3.32 DefClassFunction) ensures via 3.29 DefHasConcentratedValues that for each A in Dom(V) with set value V(A), there is a unique pair (A, y) in V, which by 3.25 DefValueAtArg (V(A) = U{s | (A, s) in V} = U{y} = y) forces y = V(A) and rules out non-functional multi-pair encodings. In 3.88-3.90, VStageLaws(V) is carried as an explicit antecedent hypothesis (and constructed bottom-up via 3.91-3.98 TransfiniteRec(VonNeumannStepG)).

entries.name: DefSetRankLaws
entries.title: Mirimanoff-von Neumann set rank recursion laws
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(R:Class)∀(V:Class)(SetRankLaws(R,V)←→((∀(x:Class)((x set)—→Ord(R(x))))∧((∀(x:Class)((x set)—→(R(x)=⋃{z|∃(y:Class)((y∈x)∧(z=(R(y)∪{R(y)})))})))∧∀(x:Class)((x set)—→(x∈V((R(x)∪{R(x)}))))))))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefSetRankLaws, PKernelDef_prf): SetRankLaws(R, V) characterizes the set rank operator valOf(R, x) and its cumulative-stage bounding law x in valOf(V, valOf(R, x) u {valOf(R, x)}) for every set x.

entries.name: DefSetRankGraph
entries.title: Canonical Mirimanoff-von Neumann set rank graph
entries.formula_unicode_html: (SetRankGraph=⋂{R|(R class-function)∧SetRankLaws(R,VStageGraph)})
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefSetRankGraph, PKernelDef_prf): SetRankGraph is the intersection of all class-functions R satisfying SetRankLaws(R, VStageGraph). Restricting R to class-functions (3.32 DefClassFunction) ensures via 3.29 DefHasConcentratedValues and 3.25 DefValueAtArg (U{y} = y) that each set x in Dom(R) is paired with the unique value y = R(x). In 3.89-3.90, SetRankLaws(R, V) is carried as an explicit antecedent hypothesis on the rank operator R.

entries.name: ThmUniverseInterOnIsOrdinal
entries.title: Step 0 of U = V_(U n On): the ordinal trace U n On of a universe is an ordinal
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(U:Class)((U universe)—→Ord((U∩On))))
entries.comment: Kernel proof term (thm_step0_universe_inter_on_is_ordinal : Thm, accompanied in universe_definitions.ML by thm_step0_universe_emptyset_in_u : ∀(U:Class)((U universe) —→ ((∅ ∈ U) ∧ ((∅ ∈ (U ∩ On)) ∧ ¬((U ∩ On) = ∅))))): if U is a universe, then U is transitive and On is an ordinal, so their binary intersection kappa = U n On is a transitive class of ordinals and hence an ordinal.

entries.name: ThmUniverseUnionClosedFromIndexedUnion
entries.title: Step 1a of U = V_(U n On): a transitive class closed under indexed unions is closed under unary union
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(U:Class)∀(f:Class)(((Tr(U)∧IndexedUnionClosed(U))∧((f class-function)∧((V⊆Dom(f))∧∀(a:Class)(f(a)=a))))—→∀(x:Class)((x∈U)—→(⋃x∈U))))
entries.comment: Kernel proof term (thm_step1a_union_closed_from_indexed_union : Thm): instantiating IndexedUnionClosed(U) with I = x in U and an identity class-function witness f on V yields f[x] = x c U and hence U(x) in U.

entries.name: ThmUniverseInterOnIsLimitOrdinal
entries.title: Step 1c of U = V_(U n On): the ordinal trace U n On of an union-closed universe is a nonzero limit ordinal
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(U:Class)(((U universe)∧∀(x:Class)((x∈U)—→(⋃x∈U)))—→LimitOrd((U∩On))))
entries.comment: Kernel proof term (thm_step1c_kappa_is_limit_ord : Thm): for any universe U closed under unary union, kappa = U n On is an ordinal, contains 0 (via thm_step0_universe_emptyset_in_u from ω ∈ U and Hereditary(U)), and is closed under ordinal successor B |-> B u {B} = U({B, {B}}) by pairing and union closure; therefore LimitOrd(U n On) holds.

entries.name: ThmVonNeumannStageSubUniverse
entries.title: Step 2 of U = V_(U n On): limit-stage inclusion V_(U n On) c= U from stage closure below U n On
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(V:Class)∀(U:Class)((VStageLaws(V)∧(Tr(U)∧(LimitOrd((U∩On))∧∀(B:Class)((B∈(U∩On))—→(V(B)∈U)))))—→(V((U∩On))⊆U)))
entries.comment: Kernel proof term (thm_step2_v_kappa_sub_u : Thm, accompanied in universe_definitions.ML by the base and successor step lemmas thm_step2_v_0_in_u, thm_step2_v_succ_in_u, and thm_step2_v_limit_fam_sub_u): under VStageLaws(V), Trans(U), LimitOrd(U n On), and the stage-closure premise ∀B ∈ (U n On), V(B) ∈ U, unfolding the limit clause V(U n On) = U_{B ∈ U n On} V(B) and applying transitivity of U yields V(U n On) c= U.

entries.name: ThmUniverseSubVonNeumannStage
entries.title: Step 3 of U = V_(U n On): rank-bounded inclusion U c= V_(U n On) from stage and rank closure
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(V:Class)∀(R:Class)∀(U:Class)((VStageLaws(V)∧(SetRankLaws(R,V)∧(LimitOrd((U∩On))∧((∀(B:Class)((B∈(U∩On))—→(V(B)∈U)))∧∀(x:Class)((x∈U)—→(R(x)∈U))))))—→(U⊆V((U∩On)))))
entries.comment: Kernel proof term (thm_step3_u_sub_v_kappa : Thm, accompanied in universe_definitions.ML by the inductive rank-successor step lemma thm_step3_rank_succ_in_u): under VStageLaws(V), SetRankLaws(R, V), LimitOrd(U n On), stage closure ∀B ∈ (U n On), V(B) ∈ U, and rank closure ∀x ∈ U, R(x) ∈ U, every a ∈ U has R(a) ∈ (U n On), R(a) u {R(a)} ∈ (U n On) by limit closure, and a ∈ V(R(a) u {R(a)}) c= V(U n On), concluding U c= V(U n On).

entries.name: ThmUniverseEqVonNeumannStageInterOn
entries.title: Conclusion of U = V_(U n On): combining Step 1c, Step 2, and Step 3 under stage, rank, and union closure
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(U:Class)((VStageLaws(VStageGraph)∧(SetRankLaws(SetRankGraph,VStageGraph)∧(((U universe)∧∀(x:Class)((x∈U)—→(⋃x∈U)))∧((∀(B:Class)((B∈(U∩On))—→(VStageGraph(B)∈U)))∧∀(x:Class)((x∈U)—→(SetRankGraph(x)∈U))))))—→(LimitOrd((U∩On))∧(U=VStageGraph((U∩On))))))
entries.comment: Synthesis theorem (thm_universe_eq_canonical_v_inter_on and thm_universe_eq_v_inter_on : Thm across the 45 constituent lemmas in universe_definitions.ML Section 11): given VStageLaws(VStageGraph), SetRankLaws(SetRankGraph, VStageGraph), Universe(U) with unary union closure, stage closure ∀B ∈ (U n On), V(B) ∈ U, and rank closure ∀x ∈ U, R(x) ∈ U, combines Step 1c (LimitOrd(U n On)), Step 2 (V_(U n On) c= U), and Step 3 (U c= V_(U n On)) via class equality antisymmetry (EqDef) to conclude LimitOrd(U n On) /\ (U = VStageGraph(U n On)).

entries.name: DefDomainRestriction
entries.title: Restriction of a class relation or function to a domain class
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(F:Class)∀(A:Class)(Restrict(F,A)={z|(z∈F)∧(pr1(z)∈A)}))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefDomainRestriction, PKernelDef_prf): Restrict(F, A) = { z : Class | (z in F) /\ (pr1(z) in A) } restricts a class relation or function F to arguments whose first Dunaev projection belongs to A.

entries.name: DefTransfiniteApproximation
entries.title: Transfinite recursion approximation predicate on ordinal domains
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(G:Class)∀(g:Class)(TransfiniteApprox(G,g)←→((g function)∧((Dom(g)∈On)∧∀(B:Class)∀(X:Class)(((B∈Dom(g))∧(X=Restrict(g,B)))—→(g(B)=G(X)))))))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefTransfiniteApproximation, PKernelDef_prf): TransfiniteApprox(G, g) holds iff g is a set-sized function whose domain Dom(g) belongs to On and for all B in Dom(g) and X = Restrict(g, B), valOf(g, B) = valOf(G, X).

entries.name: DefTransfiniteRecursionGraph
entries.title: Canonical transfinite recursion class-function graph on On
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(G:Class)(TransfiniteRec(G)=⋃{g|TransfiniteApprox(G,g)}))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefTransfiniteRecursionGraph, PKernelDef_prf): TransfiniteRec(G) = U { g : Class | TransfiniteApprox(G, g) } is the union of the class A(G) of all set-sized transfinite approximations for generator G.

entries.name: DefVonNeumannStepGenerator
entries.title: Von Neumann cumulative hierarchy transfinite step generator
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(f:Class)(VonNeumannStepG(f)=⋃{Y|∃(B:Class)((B∈Dom(f))∧(Y=𝒫(f(B))))}))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefVonNeumannStepGenerator, PKernelDef_prf): VonNeumannStepG(f) = U { Y : Class | exists (B:Class), (B in Dom(f)) /\ (Y = Pow(valOf(f, B))) } maps any set-sized ordinal approximation f to the union of the powersets of its values.

entries.name: ThmTransfiniteApproxCoherence
entries.title: Step 1 of Transfinite Recursion on On: coherence of approximations on common ordinal domains
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(G:Class)∀(g:Class)∀(h:Class)∀(A:Class)((TransfiniteApprox(G,g)∧(TransfiniteApprox(G,h)∧((∀(z:Class)((g(pr1(z))=h(pr1(z)))—→((z∈g)←→(z∈h))))∧(A∈(Dom(g)∩Dom(h))))))—→((Restrict(g,A)=Restrict(h,A))∧((g(A)=G(Restrict(g,A)))∧(g(A)=h(A))))))
entries.comment: Kernel proof term (thm_transfinite_approx_coherence and thm_transfinite_approx_coherence_step : Thm): proved by transfinite epsilon-induction (EpsIndAx) on K_1 = { B : Class | (B in (Dom(g) n Dom(h))) -> (valOf(g, B) = valOf(h, B)) } using transitivity of the ordinal intersection Dom(g) n Dom(h) (thm_bininter_transitive) and extensional restriction equality (thm_restrict_eq_from_below under graph value-extensionality forall z, (g(pr1(z)) = h(pr1(z))) -> ((z in g)  (z in h))), concluding Restrict(g, A) = Restrict(h, A) and valOf(g, A) = valOf(G, Restrict(g, A)) = valOf(h, A) for all A in Dom(g) n Dom(h).

entries.name: ThmTransfiniteRecursionEquation
entries.title: Steps 2 and 3 of Transfinite Recursion on On: approximation sethood, union inclusion, and global recursion equation F(A) = G(Restrict(F, A)) from witnessing approximations
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(G:Class)∀(g:Class)∀(F:Class)∀(A:Class)((TransfiniteApprox(G,g)—→((g set)∧(g⊆TransfiniteRec(G))))∧(((∀(B:Class)((B∈On)—→∃(h:Class)(TransfiniteApprox(G,h)∧((B∈Dom(h))∧((F(B)=h(B))∧(Restrict(F,B)=Restrict(h,B)))))))∧(A∈On))—→(F(A)=G(Restrict(F,A))))))
entries.comment: Kernel proof term (thm_transfinite_recursion_equation, thm_approx_is_set, thm_in_approx_class_iff, thm_approx_sub_transfinite_rec, and thm_restrict_agree_from_sub : Thm): proves (1) unconditionally that every G-approximation g is a set and a subclass of TransfiniteRec(G) = U { g | TransfiniteApprox(G, g) }, and (2) conditionally that whenever each ordinal B in On has a witnessing approximation h in A(G) with B in Dom(h), F(B) = h(B), and Restrict(F, B) = Restrict(h, B), the global recursion equation valOf(F, A) = valOf(G, Restrict(F, A)) holds for all A in On.

entries.name: ThmTransfiniteRecursionUniqueness
entries.title: Step 4 of Transfinite Recursion on On: uniqueness of the transfinite recursion class-function
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(G:Class)∀(F:Class)∀(H:Class)∀(A:Class)((((∀(B:Class)∀(X:Class)(((B∈On)∧(X=Restrict(F,B)))—→(F(B)=G(X))))∧∀(B:Class)∀(X:Class)(((B∈On)∧(X=Restrict(H,B)))—→(H(B)=G(X))))∧((∀(z:Class)((F(pr1(z))=H(pr1(z)))—→((z∈F)←→(z∈H))))∧(A∈On)))—→((Restrict(F,A)=Restrict(H,A))∧(F(A)=H(A)))))
entries.comment: Kernel proof term (thm_transfinite_recursion_uniqueness and thm_transfinite_recursion_uniqueness_step : Thm): proved by genuine transfinite epsilon-induction (EpsIndAx) on K_4 = { B : Class | (B in On) -> (valOf(F, B) = valOf(H, B)) } using transitivity of On (thm_on_is_transitive) and extensional restriction equality (thm_restrict_eq_from_below under graph value-extensionality forall z, (F(pr1(z)) = H(pr1(z))) -> ((z in F)  (z in H))), concluding Restrict(F, A) = Restrict(H, A) and valOf(F, A) = valOf(H, A) for all A in On.

entries.name: ThmVonNeumannHierarchyByTransfiniteRecursion
entries.title: Application of Transfinite Recursion on On: base-stage law and unfolding of VonNeumannStepG(f) = U_(B in A) P(V_B)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(f:Class)∀(V:Class)∀(A:Class)(((∀(B:Class)¬(B∈Dom(f)))—→(VonNeumannStepG(f)=∅))∧(((V(A)=VonNeumannStepG(f))∧((Dom(f)=A)∧∀(B:Class)((B∈A)—→(f(B)=V(B)))))—→((VonNeumannStepG(f)=⋃{Y|∃(B:Class)((B∈A)∧(Y=𝒫(V(B))))})∧(V(A)=⋃{Y|∃(B:Class)((B∈A)∧(Y=𝒫(V(B))))})))))
entries.comment: Kernel proof term (thm_von_neumann_hierarchy_by_recursion, thm_von_neumann_step_g_empty, thm_von_neumann_step_g_on_stage, and thm_power_cong : Thm): proves (1) unconditionally that VonNeumannStepG(f) = ∅ whenever Dom(f) is empty, and (2) conditionally, by unfolding DefVonNeumannStepGenerator and applying powerclass congruence (thm_power_cong: P = Q -> Pow(P) = Pow(Q)), that whenever Dom(f) = A, f agrees with V on A, and V(A) = VonNeumannStepG(f), both VonNeumannStepG(f) and V(A) equal U { Y : Class | exists (B:Class), (B in A) /\ (Y = Pow(valOf(V, B))) }.

entries.name: DefPowerClass
entries.title: Powerclass operator
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(K:Class)(𝒫(K)={x|x⊆K}))
entries.comment: Conservative class-operator definition (DefPowerClass, def_power_class_cert in 06_definitions.ML, PKernelDef_prf): defines the powerclass 𝒫(K) = { x : Class | x ⊆ K } of any class K as the comprehension class of all set subclasses of K. Paired with the power-set sethood axiom 3.13 AxmExponent (∀(X:Class)((X set) —→ (𝒫(X) set))).

entries.name: AxmUnion
entries.title: Union axiom: the union of a set is a set
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(x:Class)((x set)—→(⋃x set)))
entries.comment: Primitive kernel rule UnionSetAx for now, although it is derivable: Azriel Levy (On Von Neumann's Axiom System for Set Theory, Amer. Math. Monthly 75, 1968) derives it from limitation of size, powerset, heredity and pairing; see the theorem 'union of a set is a set' (thm:unionisset) in foundations/080_azriel_levi_union_thm.tex. When that derivation is formalised in the kernel, this entry becomes a theorem.

sections.title: 4. Metalogical Laws (4.01-4.08)
sections.description: Explicit substitution, context encoding, co-necessitation, uniqueness quantifiers, and reflected comprehension.

entries.name: DefMetaInstantiation
entries.title: Instantiation
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Type)∀(G:Ctx.Expression)∀(𝛗:Fm)∀(t:eval(A).Expression)∀(v:Variable)(𝘞,⟦G⟧⊢‹(∀(⦃v⦄:⟦A⟧)⟦𝛗⟧)—→⟦𝛗⟧⦇⟦t⟧/⦃v⦄⦈›))
entries.comment: Postulated +1 metalevel universal instantiation schema (requiring Fm.FFI(t, v, φ) as enforced in IncompletenessMechanization.law_4_01_meta_instantiation), accompanied by a kernel-checked object-level instance (thm_4_01_meta_instantiation / sequent_4_01_instantiation : Thm, checked by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check).

entries.name: DefMetaGeneralisation
entries.title: Generalisation
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Type)∀(Γ:Ctx)∀(𝛗:Fm)∀(v:Variable)((¬Ctx.IFV(v,Γ))—→((𝘞,Γ⊢𝛗)—→(𝘞,Γ⊢‹∀(⦃v⦄:⟦A⟧)⟦𝛗⟧›))))
entries.comment: Postulated +1 metalevel context-indexed generalisation schema with explicit context freshness guard ¬Ctx.IFV(v, Γ), accompanied by a kernel-checked object-level instance (thm_4_02_meta_generalisation / sequent_4_02_generalisation : Thm). (A theory 𝘞 is assumed here to contain only closed axioms without free variables, so v has no free occurrences in 𝘞 whenever ¬Ctx.IFV(v, Γ) holds.)

entries.name: DefMetaConecessitation
entries.title: CoNecessitation
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(Γ:Ctx)∀(𝛗:Fm)((𝘍,[]⊢‹𝘍,Γ⊢𝛗›)—→(𝘍,Γ⊢𝛗)))
entries.comment: If a formula  is derived in 𝘍 from the empty context, then the formula 𝛗 is derived in 𝘍 from the context Γ. Why this holds for 𝘍: for an arbitrary theory 𝘞, concluding (𝘞, Γ⊢𝛗) from (𝘞, [] ⊢ ) requires 1-consistency / Σ₁-soundness of 𝘞 (and for the r.e. base theory 𝘛, asserting internal co-necessitation would by Löb's theorem 5.01 trivialize 𝘛). Because 𝘍 is a non-r.e. theory of the intended model equipped with Soundness 3.72 ((𝘍, [] ⊢ ψ) → ⟦ψ⟧), instantiating 3.72 at ψ :=  directly yields (𝘍, Γ⊢𝛗).

entries.name: DefAtMostOneBinder
entries.title: Quantifier “unique”
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(𝛗:Fm)((!(z:Class)⟦𝛗⟧)←→(∀(x:Class)∀(y:Class)((⟦𝛗⟧⦇x/z⦈∧⟦𝛗⟧⦇y/z⦈)—→(x=y)))))
entries.comment: Definitional metalevel schema for the at-most-one binder (!(z:Class)φ), subject to the variable freshness and capture-avoidance side conditions x ≠ y, ¬Fm.IFV(x, φ), ¬Fm.IFV(y, φ), Fm.FFI(x, z, φ), and Fm.FFI(y, z, φ) (enforced in IncompletenessMechanization.law_4_04_at_most_one_binder_def and accompanied by the class-level witness DefAtMostOneMember / sequent_4_04_at_most_one : Thm).

entries.name: DefExistsUniqueBinder
entries.title: Quantifier “exists and unique”
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(𝛗:Fm)(𝘛,[]⊢‹(∃!(x:Class)⟦𝛗⟧)←→((∃(x:Class)⟦𝛗⟧)∧!(x:Class)⟦𝛗⟧)›))
entries.comment: Kernel-verified exists-unique binder definition (thm_4_05_exists_unique_binder : Thm, checked by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check).

entries.name: AxmMetaClassComprehension
entries.title: Class comprehension axiom schema

entries.name: DefReducedVarSubst
entries.title: Reduced variable-substitution operator on classes SubstVar(t, x, v)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(t:Class)∀(x:Class)∀(v:Class)(SubstVar(t,x,v)={u|((v=x)∧(u∈t))∨((¬(v=x))∧(u∈v))}))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefReducedVarSubst, PKernelDef_prf): SubstVar(t, x, v) = { u : Class | (((v = x) /\ (u in t)) \/ ((~(v = x)) /\ (u in v))) }, the class conditional IF v = x THEN t ELSE v FI on arbitrary classes, with the arguments in the substitution order (what t, instead of what x, where v). It is intended as the atomic case of substitution applied to codes of variables; that link through Enc is not formalised, so SubstVar is a class operation, not syntactic substitution (FACTBOOK section 4).

entries.name: ThmReducedVarSubstLaws

entries.comment: Kernel theorem thm_reduced_var_subst_laws, for arbitrary classes: the hit law (v = x) -> (SubstVar(t, x, v) = t), the miss law (~(v = x)) -> (SubstVar(t, x, v) = v), SubstVar(x, x, v) = v and SubstVar(a, x, x) = a.

entries.name: DefCardinality
entries.title: Class cardinality
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(K:Class)(|K|=(On∩⋂{a|(a∈On)∧(K≼a)})))
entries.comment: Defines the von Neumann initial-ordinal cardinality |K| = On ∩ ⋂{ a : Class | (a ∈ On) ∧ (K ≼ a) }: the intersection ⋂ of the class of all ordinal sets a ∈ On into which K injects (K ≼ a), intersected with On. Because the intersection of a non-empty class of ordinals is its least element, |K| equals the least ordinal a ∈ On with K ≼ a (the initial ordinal of K) when K is a well-orderable set, and equals On ∩ ⋂∅ = On ∩ V = On when no ordinal set a ∈ On satisfies K ≼ a (i.e., when K is a proper class). Paired in the kernel with CardLessOrderAx (PCardLessOrderAx_prf in 06_definitions.ML: ∀A∀B((|A| ≺ |B|) ⟷ (A ≺ B))).

entries.comment: Strict cardinality order A ≺ B ⟷ ¬(B ≼ A). Paired in the kernel with the cardinal-order reflection rule CardLessOrderAx (PCardLessOrderAx_prf in 06_definitions.ML: ∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)((|A| ≺ |B|) ⟷ (A ≺ B))), which embodies the Global Choice / von Neumann cardinal-equipollence principle |K| ≈ K connecting 3.41 DefCardinality with 3.43 AxmSizeLimitation.

Combined with the kernel's cardinal-order reflection rule CardLessOrderAx (PCardLessOrderAx_prf: (|A| ≺ |B|) ⟷ (A ≺ B), reflecting Global Choice V ≈ On), this yields (X ∈ V) ⟷ (X ≺ V) and hence Tight(V) in 3.69.

entries.name: DefOmega
entries.title: The intersection class of all successor-inductive (Peano-inductive) classes is called omega (⊆-minimal successor-inductive class and smallest successor-inductive ordinal)
entries.status: Definitional (Conservative Under Set Existence, Kernel AST)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(x:Class)((x∈ω)←→(∀(Q:Class)(Ind(Q)—→(x∈Q)))))
entries.comment: By definition, ω is not only the smallest successor-inductive ordinal, but also the ⊆-minimal (least) element among all successor-inductive (Peano-inductive) classes in the subclass (⊆) order (Ind(ω) ∧ ∀(Q:Class), Ind(Q) —→ (ω ⊆ Q)), directly expressing simple countable mathematical (Peano) induction up to ω. Conservativity & Sethood Note: because (x ∈ Q) implies (x set) by 3.02 DefIsSet whenever at least one inductive class Q exists (such as On in 3.60 or ω under 3.57 AxmOmegaIsSet), the unguarded RHS ∀(Q:Class)(Ind(Q) —→ x ∈ Q) is equivalent in MKTD1-theory to the strict comprehension form ((x set) ∧ ∀(Q:Class)(Ind(Q) —→ x ∈ Q)); however, in a subtheory without set-existence axioms, omitting (x set) on the RHS makes ∅ ∈ ω (and hence ∅ set) derivable from DefOmega and DefInductiveClass alone. In our kernel proofs (universe_definitions.ML), ∅ set is derived explicitly from 3.57 AxmOmegaIsSet (ω set), 3.07 (∅ ⊆ ω), and 3.12 AxmHeredity. Similarly, the set-restricted intersection ω = ⋂{q | Ind(q)} over inductive sets q agrees with the general intersection over all inductive classes Q once an inductive set exists by 3.57 AxmOmegaIsSet. | Special Def.: ω = ⋂{q | Ind(q)} (set-restricted intersection over inductive sets, equivalent to the general form once an inductive set exists by 3.57 AxmOmegaIsSet); General Def.: ∀(x:Class), (x ∈ ω) ⟷ (∀(Q:Class), Ind(Q) —→ (x ∈ Q)).

entries.name: ThmOmegaCardinal
entries.title: ω is cardinal
entries.formula_unicode_html: Card(ω)
entries.comment: Kernel proof term thm_3_65_omega_cardinal (types/omega_cardinal.ML, exact statement Card(ω)): by 3.64 DefIsCardinal with K := ω it suffices that |ω| = ω (3.41 DefCardinality). |ω| ⊆ ω because ω ≼ ω, witnessed by the identity {p | ∃k((k ∈ ω) ∧ (p = (k, k)))}, an injective class function (Dunaev pairs of sets are sets, as subclasses of 𝒫⁴(k)). ω ⊆ |ω| combines two inductions: every ordinal a satisfies n ∈ a or a ⊆ n for n ∈ ω (EpsIndAx), and the finite pigeonhole principle ¬(ω ≼ n) for n ∈ ω (induction on n over classes X with no ∈-maximal element, so no new functions are built).

entries.name: ThmOrdinalsCardinal
entries.title: On is a cardinal class
entries.formula_unicode_html: Card(On)
entries.comment: Kernel proof term (thm_3_66_on_card_sub_on : Thm with exact statement equality): proves (On cardinal) by taking K := V as the witness in 3.64 DefIsCardinal (∃K(|K| = On)). For every a ∈ S_V = {a | (a ∈ On) ∧ (V ≼ a)}, a ∈ On implies a set (3.02 DefIsSet) and hence a ∈ V (3.05 DefUniversalClass), which by 3.43 AxmSizeLimitation (PSizeLimAx_prf), CardLessOrderAx (PCardLessOrderAx_prf), and 3.42 DefCardLess yields a ≺ V ⟷ ¬(V ≼ a), contradicting V ≼ a. Hence S_V is empty, every x ∈ On belongs to ⋂S_V (3.20 DefUnaryIntersection), |V| = On ∩ ⋂S_V = On (3.41 DefCardinality, 3.10 DefClassEq), and therefore Card(On) holds.

entries.comment: Soundness of the non-r.e. theory of the intended model 𝘍: if (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ), then ⟦φ⟧ holds in the fixed background model M. Two-Level Stratification (How the Kernel Excludes TpHolds(IpFau, ...) from Object-Level Fm₀): In MKTD1-system (FACTBOOK section 6 (metalevels)), object-level set/class formulas live at metalevel 0 (sort Fm₀, enforced in the kernel by KernelDefinitions.is_object_level_fm0 in newchecker/06_definitions.ML and checked on every PComprAx_prf class comprehension node in newchecker/07_theorems.ML), which explicitly rejects TpHolds, EEval, TpFFI, TpIFV, and TpCtxIFV inside object-level class comprehension {x | φ} and object-level predicate/class definitions. Because 3.72-3.74 and 4.03 live at metalevel +1 and TpHolds(IpFau, ...) is barred from Fm₀ comprehension by is_object_level_fm0, the object-level diagonal lemma cannot be applied to (𝘍, [] ⊢ ·) to form a Tarski liar sentence or a Löb fixed point ψ ⟷ ((𝘍, [] ⊢ ψ) —→ φ).

entries.name: AxmSemanticCompletenessOfFullTheory
entries.title: Semantic Completeness of the theory 𝘍
entries.status: Metatheorem (Holds by the Definition of F, Not a Kernel Rule)
entries.prf_constructor: (metatheorem: holds by the definition of F; not a kernel rule)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(𝛗:Fm)(eval(𝛗)—→(𝘍,[]⊢𝛗)))
entries.comment: Semantic completeness (omniscience, 3.73) of the non-r.e. theory of the intended model 𝘍 at metalevel 1: for every object-level sentence φ : Fm, if φ evaluates to true in the background model M (⟦φ⟧), then φ is formally derivable in 𝘍 (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ). It holds by the definition of 𝘍 as the theory of the intended model (FACTBOOK section 2) and is a metatheorem, not a kernel rule. Stated separately from syntactic negation-completeness (3.74 AxmNegationCompletenessOfFullTheory, which is stated purely in terms of ⊢ and ¬ without mentioning ⟦φ⟧): neither implies the other in isolation, while under Soundness of 𝘍 (3.72) and classical model bivalence (⟦φ⟧ ∨ ⟦¬φ⟧) they are conditionally equivalent.

entries.name: AxmNegationCompletenessOfFullTheory
entries.title: Negation-Completeness of the theory 𝘍
entries.status: Metatheorem (Holds by the Definition of F, Not a Kernel Rule)
entries.prf_constructor: (metatheorem: holds by the definition of F; not a kernel rule)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(𝛗:Fm)((¬(𝘍,[]⊢‹¬𝛗›))—→(𝘍,[]⊢𝛗)))
entries.comment: Syntactic negation-completeness (3.74) of the non-r.e. theory of the intended model 𝘍 at metalevel 1: for every object-level sentence φ : Fm, if ¬φ is not derivable in 𝘍 (¬(𝘍, [] ⊢ ¬φ)), then φ is derivable in 𝘍 (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ). Formulated as a separate purely syntactic axiom from semantic completeness / omniscience (3.73 AxmSemanticCompletenessOfFullTheory): in classical logic, 3.74 is equivalent to (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ) ∨ (𝘍, [] ⊢ ¬φ), and becomes equivalent to semantic completeness (3.73) when combined with Soundness of 𝘍 (3.72) and classical bivalence of M (⟦φ⟧ ∨ ⟦¬φ⟧).

entries.name: DefDunaevOrderedPair
entries.title: Ordered pair(Dunaev's tagged class pair)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)((A,B)=(({{∅,{∅}}}∪{x|∃(a:Class)((a∈A)∧(x={{{{a}}},{∅}}))})∪({{∅,{∅,{∅}}}}∪{x|∃(a:Class)((a∈B)∧(x={{{{a}}},{∅,{∅}}}))}))))
entries.comment: Primitive-expanded form of Dunaev's tagged class ordered pair (A,B) = mark(A,1) ∪ mark(B,2) from 3.51 DefClassLists (with 0 = ∅, 1 = {∅}, 2 = {∅, {∅}} and tagged elements {{{{a}}}, n} = { {{{a}}}, n }), sound for arbitrary proper classes A, B (unlike the set-restricted Kuratowski pair in 3.52). Used as the canonical ordered pair (A, B) across class-level definitions (3.38, 3.77, 3.78, 3.91).

entries.name: ThmDunaevFirstProjection
entries.title: First projection of Dunaev's tagged ordered pair
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)({a|{{{{a}}},{∅}}∈(A,B)}=A))
entries.comment: Kernel proof term (thm_3_77_dunaev_pr1_sub : Thm with exact statement equality): recovers A from Dunaev's tagged ordered pair (A, B) via tag 1 = {∅} ({ a | {{{{a}}}, {∅}} ∈ (A, B) } = A, matching pr1 in 3.51 DefClassLists and 3.91 DefDomainRestriction) without requiring A or B to be sets, and together with 3.78 yields Dunaev pair injectivity (thm_dunaev_opair_injective : (A, B) = (C, D) —→ (A = C ∧ B = D)).

entries.name: ThmDunaevSecondProjection
entries.title: Second projection of Dunaev's tagged ordered pair
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)({b|{{{{b}}},{∅,{∅}}}∈(A,B)}=B))
entries.comment: Kernel proof term (thm_3_78_dunaev_pr2_sub : Thm with exact statement equality): recovers B from Dunaev's tagged ordered pair (A, B) via tag 2 = {∅, {∅}} ({ b | {{{{b}}}, {∅, {∅}}} ∈ (A, B) } = B, matching pr2 in 3.51 DefClassLists) without requiring A or B to be sets, and together with 3.77 yields Dunaev pair injectivity (thm_dunaev_opair_injective : (A, B) = (C, D) —→ (A = C ∧ B = D)).

entries.name: DefLimitOrdinal
entries.title: Nonzero limit ordinal predicate
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Class)(LimitOrd(A)←→(Ord(A)∧((¬(A=∅))∧∀(B:Class)((B∈A)—→((B∪{B})∈A))))))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefLimitOrd, PKernelDef_prf): a class A is a nonzero limit ordinal (LimitOrd(A)) iff A is an ordinal, A is non-empty, and for every B in A, the von Neumann successor B u {B} also belongs to A.

entries.name: DefIndexedUnionClosed
entries.title: Indexed-union closure predicate
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(U:Class)(IndexedUnionClosed(U)←→(∀(I:Class)∀(f:Class)(((I∈U)∧((f class-function)∧((I⊆Dom(f))∧(f[I]⊆U))))—→(⋃f[I]∈U)))))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefIndexedUnionClosed, PKernelDef_prf): a class U is closed under indexed unions (IndexedUnionClosed(U)) iff for every index set I in U and every class-function f with I c Dom(f) and relational image f[I] c U, the union U(f[I]) belongs to U.

entries.name: DefVonNeumannStageLaws
entries.title: Von Neumann cumulative hierarchy recursion laws
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(V:Class)(VStageLaws(V)←→((V(∅)=∅)∧((∀(A:Class)(Ord(A)—→(V((A∪{A}))=𝒫(V(A)))))∧((∀(A:Class)(LimitOrd(A)—→(V(A)=⋃{Y|∃(B:Class)((B∈A)∧(Y=V(B)))})))∧∀(A:Class)(Ord(A)—→((A=∅)∨((∃(B:Class)((B∈A)∧(A=(B∪{B}))))∨LimitOrd(A)))))))))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefVonNeumannStageLaws, PKernelDef_prf): VStageLaws(V) characterizes the transfinite recursion equations for the von Neumann cumulative hierarchy stages valOf(V, A) across base stage 0, successor ordinals A u {A}, and limit ordinals, together with the three-way ordinal classification (zero, successor, or limit). (Notational convention: here and in 3.82, 3.83, 3.88, 3.89, 3.98, the bound class variable V : Class, rendered in yellow in HTML and applied as V(A), denotes a candidate stage operator, distinguished by binding, tooltip, and arity from the 0-ary universal class constant V of 3.05 and 3.86.)

entries.name: DefVonNeumannStageGraph
entries.title: Canonical von Neumann cumulative hierarchy graph
entries.formula_unicode_html: (VStageGraph=⋂{V|(V class-function)∧VStageLaws(V)})
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefVonNeumannStageGraph, PKernelDef_prf): VStageGraph is the intersection of all class-functions V satisfying VStageLaws(V). Restricting V to class-functions (3.32 DefClassFunction) ensures via 3.29 DefHasConcentratedValues that for each A in Dom(V) with set value V(A), there is a unique pair (A, y) in V, which by 3.25 DefValueAtArg (V(A) = U{s | (A, s) in V} = U{y} = y) forces y = V(A) and rules out non-functional multi-pair encodings. In 3.88-3.90, VStageLaws(V) is carried as an explicit antecedent hypothesis (and constructed bottom-up via 3.91-3.98 TransfiniteRec(VonNeumannStepG)).

entries.name: DefSetRankLaws
entries.title: Mirimanoff-von Neumann set rank recursion laws
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(R:Class)∀(V:Class)(SetRankLaws(R,V)←→((∀(x:Class)((x set)—→Ord(R(x))))∧((∀(x:Class)((x set)—→(R(x)=⋃{z|∃(y:Class)((y∈x)∧(z=(R(y)∪{R(y)})))})))∧∀(x:Class)((x set)—→(x∈V((R(x)∪{R(x)}))))))))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefSetRankLaws, PKernelDef_prf): SetRankLaws(R, V) characterizes the set rank operator valOf(R, x) and its cumulative-stage bounding law x in valOf(V, valOf(R, x) u {valOf(R, x)}) for every set x.

entries.name: DefSetRankGraph
entries.title: Canonical Mirimanoff-von Neumann set rank graph
entries.formula_unicode_html: (SetRankGraph=⋂{R|(R class-function)∧SetRankLaws(R,VStageGraph)})
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefSetRankGraph, PKernelDef_prf): SetRankGraph is the intersection of all class-functions R satisfying SetRankLaws(R, VStageGraph). Restricting R to class-functions (3.32 DefClassFunction) ensures via 3.29 DefHasConcentratedValues and 3.25 DefValueAtArg (U{y} = y) that each set x in Dom(R) is paired with the unique value y = R(x). In 3.89-3.90, SetRankLaws(R, V) is carried as an explicit antecedent hypothesis on the rank operator R.

entries.name: ThmUniverseInterOnIsOrdinal
entries.title: Step 0 of U = V_(U n On): the ordinal trace U n On of a universe is an ordinal
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(U:Class)((U universe)—→Ord((U∩On))))
entries.comment: Kernel proof term (thm_step0_universe_inter_on_is_ordinal : Thm, accompanied in universe_definitions.ML by thm_step0_universe_emptyset_in_u : ∀(U:Class)((U universe) —→ ((∅ ∈ U) ∧ ((∅ ∈ (U ∩ On)) ∧ ¬((U ∩ On) = ∅))))): if U is a universe, then U is transitive and On is an ordinal, so their binary intersection kappa = U n On is a transitive class of ordinals and hence an ordinal.

entries.name: ThmUniverseUnionClosedFromIndexedUnion
entries.title: Step 1a of U = V_(U n On): a transitive class closed under indexed unions is closed under unary union
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(U:Class)∀(f:Class)(((Tr(U)∧IndexedUnionClosed(U))∧((f class-function)∧((V⊆Dom(f))∧∀(a:Class)(f(a)=a))))—→∀(x:Class)((x∈U)—→(⋃x∈U))))
entries.comment: Kernel proof term (thm_step1a_union_closed_from_indexed_union : Thm): instantiating IndexedUnionClosed(U) with I = x in U and an identity class-function witness f on V yields f[x] = x c U and hence U(x) in U.

entries.name: ThmUniverseInterOnIsLimitOrdinal
entries.title: Step 1c of U = V_(U n On): the ordinal trace U n On of an union-closed universe is a nonzero limit ordinal
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(U:Class)(((U universe)∧∀(x:Class)((x∈U)—→(⋃x∈U)))—→LimitOrd((U∩On))))
entries.comment: Kernel proof term (thm_step1c_kappa_is_limit_ord : Thm): for any universe U closed under unary union, kappa = U n On is an ordinal, contains 0 (via thm_step0_universe_emptyset_in_u from ω ∈ U and Hereditary(U)), and is closed under ordinal successor B |-> B u {B} = U({B, {B}}) by pairing and union closure; therefore LimitOrd(U n On) holds.

entries.name: ThmVonNeumannStageSubUniverse
entries.title: Step 2 of U = V_(U n On): limit-stage inclusion V_(U n On) c= U from stage closure below U n On
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(V:Class)∀(U:Class)((VStageLaws(V)∧(Tr(U)∧(LimitOrd((U∩On))∧∀(B:Class)((B∈(U∩On))—→(V(B)∈U)))))—→(V((U∩On))⊆U)))
entries.comment: Kernel proof term (thm_step2_v_kappa_sub_u : Thm, accompanied in universe_definitions.ML by the base and successor step lemmas thm_step2_v_0_in_u, thm_step2_v_succ_in_u, and thm_step2_v_limit_fam_sub_u): under VStageLaws(V), Trans(U), LimitOrd(U n On), and the stage-closure premise ∀B ∈ (U n On), V(B) ∈ U, unfolding the limit clause V(U n On) = U_{B ∈ U n On} V(B) and applying transitivity of U yields V(U n On) c= U.

entries.name: ThmUniverseSubVonNeumannStage
entries.title: Step 3 of U = V_(U n On): rank-bounded inclusion U c= V_(U n On) from stage and rank closure
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(V:Class)∀(R:Class)∀(U:Class)((VStageLaws(V)∧(SetRankLaws(R,V)∧(LimitOrd((U∩On))∧((∀(B:Class)((B∈(U∩On))—→(V(B)∈U)))∧∀(x:Class)((x∈U)—→(R(x)∈U))))))—→(U⊆V((U∩On)))))
entries.comment: Kernel proof term (thm_step3_u_sub_v_kappa : Thm, accompanied in universe_definitions.ML by the inductive rank-successor step lemma thm_step3_rank_succ_in_u): under VStageLaws(V), SetRankLaws(R, V), LimitOrd(U n On), stage closure ∀B ∈ (U n On), V(B) ∈ U, and rank closure ∀x ∈ U, R(x) ∈ U, every a ∈ U has R(a) ∈ (U n On), R(a) u {R(a)} ∈ (U n On) by limit closure, and a ∈ V(R(a) u {R(a)}) c= V(U n On), concluding U c= V(U n On).

entries.name: ThmUniverseEqVonNeumannStageInterOn
entries.title: Conclusion of U = V_(U n On): combining Step 1c, Step 2, and Step 3 under stage, rank, and union closure
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(U:Class)((VStageLaws(VStageGraph)∧(SetRankLaws(SetRankGraph,VStageGraph)∧(((U universe)∧∀(x:Class)((x∈U)—→(⋃x∈U)))∧((∀(B:Class)((B∈(U∩On))—→(VStageGraph(B)∈U)))∧∀(x:Class)((x∈U)—→(SetRankGraph(x)∈U))))))—→(LimitOrd((U∩On))∧(U=VStageGraph((U∩On))))))
entries.comment: Synthesis theorem (thm_universe_eq_canonical_v_inter_on and thm_universe_eq_v_inter_on : Thm across the 45 constituent lemmas in universe_definitions.ML Section 11): given VStageLaws(VStageGraph), SetRankLaws(SetRankGraph, VStageGraph), Universe(U) with unary union closure, stage closure ∀B ∈ (U n On), V(B) ∈ U, and rank closure ∀x ∈ U, R(x) ∈ U, combines Step 1c (LimitOrd(U n On)), Step 2 (V_(U n On) c= U), and Step 3 (U c= V_(U n On)) via class equality antisymmetry (EqDef) to conclude LimitOrd(U n On) /\ (U = VStageGraph(U n On)).

entries.name: DefDomainRestriction
entries.title: Restriction of a class relation or function to a domain class
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(F:Class)∀(A:Class)(Restrict(F,A)={z|(z∈F)∧(pr1(z)∈A)}))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefDomainRestriction, PKernelDef_prf): Restrict(F, A) = { z : Class | (z in F) /\ (pr1(z) in A) } restricts a class relation or function F to arguments whose first Dunaev projection belongs to A.

entries.name: DefTransfiniteApproximation
entries.title: Transfinite recursion approximation predicate on ordinal domains
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(G:Class)∀(g:Class)(TransfiniteApprox(G,g)←→((g function)∧((Dom(g)∈On)∧∀(B:Class)∀(X:Class)(((B∈Dom(g))∧(X=Restrict(g,B)))—→(g(B)=G(X)))))))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefTransfiniteApproximation, PKernelDef_prf): TransfiniteApprox(G, g) holds iff g is a set-sized function whose domain Dom(g) belongs to On and for all B in Dom(g) and X = Restrict(g, B), valOf(g, B) = valOf(G, X).

entries.name: DefTransfiniteRecursionGraph
entries.title: Canonical transfinite recursion class-function graph on On
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(G:Class)(TransfiniteRec(G)=⋃{g|TransfiniteApprox(G,g)}))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefTransfiniteRecursionGraph, PKernelDef_prf): TransfiniteRec(G) = U { g : Class | TransfiniteApprox(G, g) } is the union of the class A(G) of all set-sized transfinite approximations for generator G.

entries.name: DefVonNeumannStepGenerator
entries.title: Von Neumann cumulative hierarchy transfinite step generator
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(f:Class)(VonNeumannStepG(f)=⋃{Y|∃(B:Class)((B∈Dom(f))∧(Y=𝒫(f(B))))}))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefVonNeumannStepGenerator, PKernelDef_prf): VonNeumannStepG(f) = U { Y : Class | exists (B:Class), (B in Dom(f)) /\ (Y = Pow(valOf(f, B))) } maps any set-sized ordinal approximation f to the union of the powersets of its values.

entries.name: ThmTransfiniteApproxCoherence
entries.title: Step 1 of Transfinite Recursion on On: coherence of approximations on common ordinal domains
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(G:Class)∀(g:Class)∀(h:Class)∀(A:Class)((TransfiniteApprox(G,g)∧(TransfiniteApprox(G,h)∧((∀(z:Class)((g(pr1(z))=h(pr1(z)))—→((z∈g)←→(z∈h))))∧(A∈(Dom(g)∩Dom(h))))))—→((Restrict(g,A)=Restrict(h,A))∧((g(A)=G(Restrict(g,A)))∧(g(A)=h(A))))))
entries.comment: Kernel proof term (thm_transfinite_approx_coherence and thm_transfinite_approx_coherence_step : Thm): proved by transfinite epsilon-induction (EpsIndAx) on K_1 = { B : Class | (B in (Dom(g) n Dom(h))) -> (valOf(g, B) = valOf(h, B)) } using transitivity of the ordinal intersection Dom(g) n Dom(h) (thm_bininter_transitive) and extensional restriction equality (thm_restrict_eq_from_below under graph value-extensionality forall z, (g(pr1(z)) = h(pr1(z))) -> ((z in g)  (z in h))), concluding Restrict(g, A) = Restrict(h, A) and valOf(g, A) = valOf(G, Restrict(g, A)) = valOf(h, A) for all A in Dom(g) n Dom(h).

entries.name: ThmTransfiniteRecursionEquation
entries.title: Steps 2 and 3 of Transfinite Recursion on On: approximation sethood, union inclusion, and global recursion equation F(A) = G(Restrict(F, A)) from witnessing approximations
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(G:Class)∀(g:Class)∀(F:Class)∀(A:Class)((TransfiniteApprox(G,g)—→((g set)∧(g⊆TransfiniteRec(G))))∧(((∀(B:Class)((B∈On)—→∃(h:Class)(TransfiniteApprox(G,h)∧((B∈Dom(h))∧((F(B)=h(B))∧(Restrict(F,B)=Restrict(h,B)))))))∧(A∈On))—→(F(A)=G(Restrict(F,A))))))
entries.comment: Kernel proof term (thm_transfinite_recursion_equation, thm_approx_is_set, thm_in_approx_class_iff, thm_approx_sub_transfinite_rec, and thm_restrict_agree_from_sub : Thm): proves (1) unconditionally that every G-approximation g is a set and a subclass of TransfiniteRec(G) = U { g | TransfiniteApprox(G, g) }, and (2) conditionally that whenever each ordinal B in On has a witnessing approximation h in A(G) with B in Dom(h), F(B) = h(B), and Restrict(F, B) = Restrict(h, B), the global recursion equation valOf(F, A) = valOf(G, Restrict(F, A)) holds for all A in On.

entries.name: ThmTransfiniteRecursionUniqueness
entries.title: Step 4 of Transfinite Recursion on On: uniqueness of the transfinite recursion class-function
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(G:Class)∀(F:Class)∀(H:Class)∀(A:Class)((((∀(B:Class)∀(X:Class)(((B∈On)∧(X=Restrict(F,B)))—→(F(B)=G(X))))∧∀(B:Class)∀(X:Class)(((B∈On)∧(X=Restrict(H,B)))—→(H(B)=G(X))))∧((∀(z:Class)((F(pr1(z))=H(pr1(z)))—→((z∈F)←→(z∈H))))∧(A∈On)))—→((Restrict(F,A)=Restrict(H,A))∧(F(A)=H(A)))))
entries.comment: Kernel proof term (thm_transfinite_recursion_uniqueness and thm_transfinite_recursion_uniqueness_step : Thm): proved by genuine transfinite epsilon-induction (EpsIndAx) on K_4 = { B : Class | (B in On) -> (valOf(F, B) = valOf(H, B)) } using transitivity of On (thm_on_is_transitive) and extensional restriction equality (thm_restrict_eq_from_below under graph value-extensionality forall z, (F(pr1(z)) = H(pr1(z))) -> ((z in F)  (z in H))), concluding Restrict(F, A) = Restrict(H, A) and valOf(F, A) = valOf(H, A) for all A in On.

entries.name: ThmVonNeumannHierarchyByTransfiniteRecursion
entries.title: Application of Transfinite Recursion on On: base-stage law and unfolding of VonNeumannStepG(f) = U_(B in A) P(V_B)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(f:Class)∀(V:Class)∀(A:Class)(((∀(B:Class)¬(B∈Dom(f)))—→(VonNeumannStepG(f)=∅))∧(((V(A)=VonNeumannStepG(f))∧((Dom(f)=A)∧∀(B:Class)((B∈A)—→(f(B)=V(B)))))—→((VonNeumannStepG(f)=⋃{Y|∃(B:Class)((B∈A)∧(Y=𝒫(V(B))))})∧(V(A)=⋃{Y|∃(B:Class)((B∈A)∧(Y=𝒫(V(B))))})))))
entries.comment: Kernel proof term (thm_von_neumann_hierarchy_by_recursion, thm_von_neumann_step_g_empty, thm_von_neumann_step_g_on_stage, and thm_power_cong : Thm): proves (1) unconditionally that VonNeumannStepG(f) = ∅ whenever Dom(f) is empty, and (2) conditionally, by unfolding DefVonNeumannStepGenerator and applying powerclass congruence (thm_power_cong: P = Q -> Pow(P) = Pow(Q)), that whenever Dom(f) = A, f agrees with V on A, and V(A) = VonNeumannStepG(f), both VonNeumannStepG(f) and V(A) equal U { Y : Class | exists (B:Class), (B in A) /\ (Y = Pow(valOf(V, B))) }.

entries.name: DefPowerClass
entries.title: Powerclass operator
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(K:Class)(𝒫(K)={x|x⊆K}))
entries.comment: Conservative class-operator definition (DefPowerClass, def_power_class_cert in 06_definitions.ML, PKernelDef_prf): defines the powerclass 𝒫(K) = { x : Class | x ⊆ K } of any class K as the comprehension class of all set subclasses of K. Paired with the power-set sethood axiom 3.13 AxmExponent (∀(X:Class)((X set) —→ (𝒫(X) set))).

entries.name: AxmUnion
entries.title: Union axiom: the union of a set is a set
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(x:Class)((x set)—→(⋃x set)))
entries.comment: Primitive kernel rule UnionSetAx for now, although it is derivable: Azriel Levy (On Von Neumann's Axiom System for Set Theory, Amer. Math. entries.name: DefMetaGeneralisation
entries.title: Generalisation
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Type)∀(Γ:Ctx)∀(𝛗:Fm)∀(v:Variable)((¬Ctx.IFV(v,Γ))—→((𝘞,Γ⊢𝛗)—→(𝘞,Γ⊢‹∀(⦃v⦄:⟦A⟧)⟦𝛗⟧›))))

(A theory 𝘞 is assumed here to contain only closed axioms without free variables, so v has no free occurrences in 𝘞 whenever ¬Ctx.IFV(v, Γ) holds.)

entries.name: DefMetaConecessitation
entries.title: CoNecessitation
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(Γ:Ctx)∀(𝛗:Fm)((𝘍,[]⊢‹𝘍,Γ⊢𝛗›)—→(𝘍,Γ⊢𝛗)))
entries.comment: If a formula  is derived in 𝘍 from the empty context, then the formula 𝛗 is derived in 𝘍 from the context Γ. Why this holds for 𝘍: for an arbitrary theory 𝘞, concluding (𝘞, Γ⊢𝛗) from (𝘞, [] ⊢ ) requires 1-consistency / Σ₁-soundness of 𝘞 (and for the r.e. base theory 𝘛, asserting internal co-necessitation would by Löb's theorem 5.01 trivialize 𝘛). Because 𝘍 is a non-r.e. theory of the intended model equipped with Soundness 3.72 ((𝘍, [] ⊢ ψ) → ⟦ψ⟧), instantiating 3.72 at ψ :=  directly yields (𝘍, Γ⊢𝛗).

entries.name: DefAtMostOneBinder
entries.title: Quantifier “unique”
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(𝛗:Fm)((!(z:Class)⟦𝛗⟧)←→(∀(x:Class)∀(y:Class)((⟦𝛗⟧⦇x/z⦈∧⟦𝛗⟧⦇y/z⦈)—→(x=y)))))

entries.name: DefReducedVarSubst
entries.title: Reduced variable-substitution operator on classes SubstVar(t, x, v)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(t:Class)∀(x:Class)∀(v:Class)(SubstVar(t,x,v)={u|((v=x)∧(u∈t))∨((¬(v=x))∧(u∈v))}))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefReducedVarSubst, PKernelDef_prf): SubstVar(t, x, v) = { u : Class | (((v = x) /\ (u in t)) \/ ((~(v = x)) /\ (u in v))) }, the class conditional IF v = x THEN t ELSE v FI on arbitrary classes, with the arguments in the substitution order (what t, instead of what x, where v). It is intended as the atomic case of substitution applied to codes of variables; that link through Enc is not formalised, so SubstVar is a class operation, not syntactic substitution (FACTBOOK section 4).

entries.name: ThmReducedVarSubstLaws
entries.title: Hit, miss, self and diagonal laws of SubstVar(t, x, v)
entries.formula_unicode_html: ((∀(t:Class)∀(x:Class)∀(v:Class)(((v=x)—→(SubstVar(t,x,v)=t))∧((¬(v=x))—→(SubstVar(t,x,v)=v))))∧((∀(x:Class)∀(v:Class)(SubstVar(x,x,v)=v))∧∀(a:Class)∀(x:Class)(SubstVar(a,x,x)=a)))
entries.comment: Kernel theorem thm_reduced_var_subst_laws, for arbitrary classes: the hit law (v = x) -> (SubstVar(t, x, v) = t), the miss law (~(v = x)) -> (SubstVar(t, x, v) = v), SubstVar(x, x, v) = v and SubstVar(a, x, x) = a.

entries.name: ThmLoeb
entries.title: Löb's theorem
entries.prf_constructor: (the linked kernel proof has a different statement; see GitLab #8101)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(𝛗:Fm)(𝘌,[]⊢‹(𝘛,[]⊢‹(𝘛,[]⊢𝛗)—→⟦𝛗⟧›)—→(𝘛,[]⊢𝛗)›))
entries.comment: Postulated, not derived: the MKTD1 kernel registers this statement as the unchecked GeneralDef ThmLoeb (general_definition_allowlist, newchecker/06_definitions.ML). An informal step-by-step trace exists only in the standalone model IncompletenessMechanization.derive_loeb_trace (incompleteness.ML), which is not connected to the kernel. Here 𝘌 ∈ {IΣ₁, PA, 𝘛, NBG, MK} is an unspecified elementary metatheory capable of proving HBL conditions D1-D3 for the r.e. base theory 𝘛 (specifically D3, formalized / internal Σ₁-completeness ψ —→ Pr_𝘛(⌜ψ⌝), which requires Σ₁-induction IΣ₁ and cannot be proved inside Robinson's arithmetic Q even though Q is externally Σ₁-complete for true Σ₁ sentences; see Hájek & Pudlák 1993; Bezboruah & Shepherdson 1976; Boolos 1993).
